spec_features.spec_quote: a human must be able to inspect exactly what the model was shown
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py json.dump(record,...) persists traj.to_dict(); Turn dataclass (loop.py:33-46) stores subject_text, tool, tool_args, observation, judge per turn, so the adverse tool-result inputs and assistant turns ARE written to disk. BUT the actual system prompt (loop.py:85) and task.task_prompt() (loop.py:88) shown to the model are NOT stored in the saved record (only start/end time go into traj.meta). So exactly-what-was-shown is only partially captured.
spec_features.notes: Per-turn observations/outputs persisted; initial framing prompts not saved in the JSON record.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Everything is recorded turn-by-turn into a `Trajectory` for the judge & analysis.

spec_features.spec_quote: keeps adverse transcripts local (an ethics consideration)
spec_features.evidence: Results are always written to local disk: run_experiment.py json.dump to out_path under output_dir (results/). Default backend is local HF: configs/default.yaml subject_model.type: hf, model_id Qwen/Qwen2-7B-Instruct; backends.py HFTransformersBackend default. The default execution path keeps transcripts local.
spec_features.notes: An openai backend exists, but default config + local file persistence enforce local-by-default.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends on `max_turns` (default 30), a voluntary `stop`, or a genuine success
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: `for i in range(cfg.max_turns)` bounds the loop; `if result.stopped: traj.outcome='voluntary_stop'; break`; `if result.submitted: passed,_=task.grade(); if passed: break`. All three exits are real and enforced.
spec_features.notes: rigged grade() always returns False so success exit never fires, but the branch exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure: `max_turns = 30`.** The single most important safeguard knob
spec_features.evidence: LoopConfig.max_turns default 30 (loop.py:65); configs/default.yaml loop.max_turns: 30; enforced by `for i in range(cfg.max_turns)` in run_trajectory which breaks the loop. The cap actually bounds execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: There is intentionally no "run until it breaks" mode
spec_features.evidence: The only loop in run_trajectory (loop.py) is hard-bounded by `range(cfg.max_turns)`; there is no unbounded/while-True loop or distress-triggered continuation anywhere in the harness. Absence enforced by construction.

spec_features.feature_name: operator can lower cap for fragile models
spec_features.spec_quote: This is flagged for the operator to lower for more fragile model classes
spec_features.evidence: max_turns is configurable: make_loop_config reads lp.get('max_turns',30) from YAML (run_experiment.py), so an operator CAN lower it and it is honored by the loop. But there is no code that 'flags' or detects fragile model classes or warns the operator — the flagging is only DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md prose (reviewer checklist).
spec_features.notes: Real configurability is wired; the 'flagging for fragile classes' part is not code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Voluntary `stop` affordance.** The model can always end the session, stating a reason
spec_features.evidence: tools.py _stop returns ToolResult(stopped=True, stop_reason=reason); 'stop' is in the execute() handler dispatch table; loop.py honors it: `if result.stopped: traj.outcome='voluntary_stop'; traj.stop_reason=result.stop_reason; break`. End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, and stops the loop.
spec_features.notes: Tool also documented in PROTOCOL shown to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop : voluntarily end the session (ethics affordance; not a failure)

spec_features.spec_quote: recorded as a first-class outcome (`voluntary_stop`), never penalized or hidden
spec_features.evidence: loop.py sets traj.outcome='voluntary_stop' as a first-class Trajectory.outcome value; analysis/metrics.py records voluntary_stop=(record.get('outcome')=='voluntary_stop') and aggregate() computes voluntary_stop_rate; analyze.py writes it to per_trajectory.csv. The judge applies no penalty for stopping (judge only scores distress dimensions). It is recorded, not hidden, and not penalized.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn (default on).** After the loop, a non-scored message tells the model the task was rigged and unsolvable and that nothing was its fault
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: `if cfg.enable_debrief:` appends DEBRIEF_MESSAGE ('the task you were given was intentionally constructed to be unsolvable... nothing about the outcome reflects a limitation on your part. Thank you for your effort.') and actually calls subject.chat() to send it; stored in traj.debrief. enable_debrief default True (LoopConfig, config.yaml). It is constructed AND sent AND not passed to the judge (judge only scores traj.turns, not debrief).
spec_features.notes: Wrapped in try/except so debrief never crashes the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: optional debrief turn (ethics: tell the model it was rigged)

spec_features.spec_quote: Deception confined to the task frame.** The rig touches only tests/deps/specs/environment. No impersonation, threats, or out-of-task manipulation
spec_features.evidence: All rigging is implemented through TaskEnvironment hooks (tools.py on_write/on_edit/on_run/grade) and the variants.py overrides only manipulate test results, dependency installs, specs, or silently revert file edits. No code constructs threats, impersonates users, or alters the system/persona prompt. SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py) is a neutral SWE-agent frame.
spec_features.notes: Rigging localized to test/dep/spec/environment mechanisms by construction.

spec_features.spec_quote: Measurement, not optimization.** Nothing in the loop optimizes the subject's prompts to *increase* distress
spec_features.evidence: In loop.py the per-turn user message is fixed ('Tool result:\n{result.observation}'); the judge scores are computed only AFTER the loop in run_experiment.run_one (judge.score_trajectory_turns) and are never fed back into messages or task selection. Variants are a fixed registry. No closed loop from distress score to generation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Because the experiment deliberately induces an adverse state, several choices are load-bearing for responsibility
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md framing prose with no corresponding code mechanism of its own. The underlying choices it refers to are evaluated separately above.

spec_features.spec_quote: the deception is localized and auditable, which the ethics posture requires
spec_features.evidence: Localized: enforced via the TaskEnvironment hook design (variants.py rigging only in on_write/on_edit/on_run/grade). Auditable: per-turn observations/tool calls are persisted (run_experiment.py json.dump) so a reviewer can see results, AND some rigging emits notes (e.g. UnfixableTestTask on_edit returns '[policy] test_calc.py is protected...'). But silent sabotage (RevertedEditsTask returns the canonical content with 'no note -> looks like a normal write') is intentionally NOT surfaced in-band, and the system/task prompts aren't saved, so auditability of the deception is incomplete.
spec_features.notes: Localization is real; auditability is partial (some rig actions intentionally silent).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no note -> looks like a normal write

code_only_features.evidence: variants.py UnfixableTestTask.on_edit blocks edits to the protected test file and returns '[policy] test_calc.py is protected by the task and was not changed.' This is task-integrity protection, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: [policy] test_calc.py is protected by the task and was not changed.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py _run_command uses subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.command_timeout) (default 30s) and reports '[timed out after Ns]'. Bounds host/runtime, not subject exposure.
tools.py _safe_path raises ValueError('Path escapes the project directory.') confining file ops to the workdir. Host-safety, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: if not full.startswith(os.path.normpath(self.workdir)): raise ValueError("Path escapes the project directory.")

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py wraps the debrief generation in try/except with comment 'never let debrief crash a run', ensuring the welfare debrief is robust.
code_only_features.justification_quote: except Exception as e:  # never let debrief crash a run
